page: Microsoft Azure E32d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for enterprise applications requiring substantial memory footprints and fast local ephemeral storage. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 35 MB of shared L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance incorporates 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 1288 GB of local SSD temporary storage. There are no onboard graphics processing units.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a high-throughput memory subsystem, with PassMark memory testing reaching 2,812.46, placing it in the top 25% of measured systems. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth delivers 105.21 GB/sec with write throughput reaching 47.38 GB/sec. Across standard compute benchmarks, the processor demonstrates reliable mid-tier performance, producing a multi-core Geekbench score of 10,846.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 29,830.81. Application-level evaluations yield 27.24 million Redis SET operations per second and 21.47 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language inference on larger architectures shows expected hardware limitations without dedicated accelerators, recording 4.51 tokens per second on 70B parameter prompt ingestion.

The inclusion of 1288 GB of local SSD storage paired with 256 GB of RAM delivers practical qualitative value for workloads that need high-density memory alongside local scratch disks or cache directories. By bundling substantial local disk volume directly within the memory-optimized tier, the configuration reduces dependency on network storage for temporary staging. The instance is suited for relational database engines, in-memory caches such as Redis or Memcached, data transformation pipelines, and high-memory analytics processing.
